purpose: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define Absolute Base Zero as the minimal boot substrate from which capabilities are added explicitly rather than assumed from a monolithic default runtime. [2] Define the boot baseline as no optional capabilities enabled by assumption: runtime composition begins from an explicit minimal base and only declared selections are added.

value.additive_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Capabilities are added through explicit configuration/profile/module selection. [2] Runtime feature composition is additive from the baseline.
value.authority_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Boot inclusion makes a capability available; it does not grant caller authorization. [2] Baseline availability remains separate from authorization.
value.baseline_rule: Optional components begin disabled/unselected unless required by the immutable minimal runtime base contract.
value.compatibility_rule: Legacy broad-default profiles require explicit migration to equivalent selected sets.
value.default_rule: Defaults, where allowed, are explicit profile data and not undocumented runtime heuristics.
value.dependency_rule: Dependencies constrain valid selections but do not auto-enable themselves.
value.implicit_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Optional capability is never active merely because its implementation exists on disk. [2] Installed, discovered, historically used or dependency-adjacent components are not implicitly enabled.
value.pruning_rule: Negative pruning may explicitly remove otherwise selected capability.
value.safety_rule: Unknown selection state resolves to unavailable/disabled rather than enabled.
